slot.brief: Photon energy / Bohr model: compare emitted photons for two transitions or two hydrogen-like species (H vs He+); set up ratio of energies or radii.

stem: What is the ratio of the energy of a photon emitted by $\text{He}^+$ in the transition $n=3\to2$ to that emitted by hydrogen in the transition $n=4\to2$?

verdicts.working: For a hydrogen-like ion, photon energy is proportional to Z²(1/n_f² − 1/n_i²). The ratio is 4(1/4 − 1/9)/(1/4 − 1/16) = 80/27.

working:
$E\propto Z^2\left(\dfrac{1}{n_f^2}-\dfrac{1}{n_i^2}\right)$. $\dfrac{E_{\text{He}^+}}{E_{\text{H}}}=\dfrac{4(\frac14-\frac19)}{\frac14-\frac1{16}}=\dfrac{80}{27}$

Independent check: For a hydrogen-like ion, photon energy is proportional to Z²(1/n_f² − 1/n_i²). The ratio is 4(1/4 − 1/9)/(1/4 − 1/16) = 80/27.
